en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Nineteenth Chapter
The Discourse on Suchness:
Is the suchness of all phenomena unconditioned? Yes.
“Nibbāna is … [and so on] … the Deathless”?
One should not say this … [and so on] …”
Is the suchness of all phenomena unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned?
Yes. Are there thus two unconditioned things?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Are there two unconditioned things? Yes.
"Are there two refuges...
[as before] ...or do they blow between them?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
Is the materiality of matter not itself unconditioned?
Yes. [Is it then] Nibbāna? ... [and so on].
Is it "the deathless"?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the nature of form (rūpatā) unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
You should not say so …pe…
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
“Does the intermediate space blow?
“One should certainly not say so…” “…Is there, in feeling, the state of being feeling? Is it not the state of being feeling? …pe…
Is perception not restrained by its own nature as perception? ...
Is volitional formations not restrained by their own nature as volitional formations? ...
Is consciousness not restrained by its own nature as consciousness? Is it not the case that the nature of consciousness is the unconditioned?
“Yes. “Is nibbāna … [and so on] … the deathless?”
It should not be said so... [as before] ...
Is not the "form-ness" of form simply form-ness? ...
Is not the "consciousness-ness" of consciousness simply consciousness-ness? And is not consciousness-ness unconditioned, while Nibbāna is unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there six unconditioned things?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Are there six unconditioned things?
Yes. There are six refuges … [and so on] …
“Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so… [as before]… It should not be said—
“Is the suchness of all phenomena unconditioned?
Yes. Is the suchness of all phenomena form? …
Feeling … perception … volitional formations …
Is it consciousness?
One should not say so.
Therefore, the suchness of all phenomena is unconditioned.
The Discussion on Suchness is finished.
